Abandoned vehicle means a machine designed to be propelled by an internal combustion engine, or by an electric motor, manufactured for the transporting of persons or property, including, without limitation, automobiles, trucks, truck trailers, motorized carts, motorcycles, mopeds, scooters and tractors, which is in an inoperative state because of being wrecked, junked, dismantled, unused or discarded. Enclosure means a structure constructed or manufactured in a manner so as to preclude any view of any portion of the interior thereof from any public street or sidewalk. Residential property means any real property located within the city designated under the zoning ordinances and maps as residential zoning districts, or any real properties located within the city which are primarily utilized to provide living quarters for one or more individuals.
Storage means the parking or leaving of an abandoned vehicle for a period of time in excess of five consecutive days.

538:
(a) As provided in O.C.G.A. § 41-2-5, the jurisdiction for the abatement of any nuisance arising out of the existence of an abandoned vehicle located on private property within the city shall be vested in the municipal court. The grant of jurisdiction made in this section is not intended, and shall not be construed to be, a grant to exclude or limit the jurisdiction of any other court of this state vested by the law of this state with jurisdiction over such proceedings.
(b) Any proceeding to abate a nuisance existing or resulting from an abandoned vehicle in storage on private property within the city shall be commenced by the chief of police of the city in the name and on the behalf of the city, or by a private citizen thereof, by the filing of a petition with the municipal court seeking the abatement thereof. The petition shall identify the property upon which the abandoned vehicle is being maintained, state the name of the person in control or possession of the real property, together with a description of the abandoned vehicle alleged to constitute such nuisance, and shall provide sufficient facts so as to inform the court as to the nature of such nuisance. If, upon the filing of such petition, the judge of the court concludes that sufficient facts are alleged to require further inquiry and proceedings as to the existence of a nuisance, an order shall be entered by the court setting a hearing date for the adjudication of the issues raised in the petition.
(c) The petition to abate the nuisance, together with a copy of the order of the court for hearing thereon, shall be served on the person in possession or control of the real property upon which the nuisance is alleged to exist at least ten days prior to the scheduled hearing date, either personally or by certified or registered mail with return receipt requested. If either the identity or location of such person is unknown, or for whatever reason such person cannot be located for such service, a copy of the petition and the order shall be conspicuously affixed to the abandoned vehicle in a manner so as to provide anyone in its vicinity with notice of the presence of such petition and order.
(d) At the scheduled hearing, the court shall hear the pertinent evidence as to the facts and circumstances surrounding the maintenance of the abandoned vehicle and shall allow the person in possession or control of the real property to present any relevant and pertinent evidence as to why same does not constitute a nuisance.
(e) If after hearing the evidence presented at the hearing the court concludes that a nuisance, within the meaning of section 34-33, exists, the court shall enter an order requiring and directing that the abandoned vehicle be removed from the corporate limits of the city within ten days of the date of the order. A copy of the order requiring the abatement of the nuisance shall be served on the person in possession or control of the real property upon which the nuisance is alleged to exist, either personally or by certified or registered mail with return receipt requested. If either the identity or location of such person is unknown, or for whatever reason the person cannot be located for the purposes of such service, a copy of the order shall be conspicuously affixed to the abandoned vehicle in a manner so as to provide anyone in its vicinity with notice of the presence of the order.
(f) If the person in control or possession of the property upon which the abandoned vehicle exists fails to remove the abandoned vehicle within the ten-day period specified by the court for the abatement of the nuisance, then and in such event the city shall remove, or cause to be removed, the abandoned vehicle from the municipal limits of the city for disposal in such a manner as will terminate the characteristics thereof which resulted in same being found to be a nuisance. The city, in the pursuit of its duties to dispose of the abandoned vehicle, shall be authorized to sell the abandoned vehicle for junk or metal salvage, and any consideration received for such sale shall be retained by the city to offset the costs and expenses incurred in the abatement of the nuisance.
(Code 1996, § 42-60)

The following acts, among others, shall constitute a violation of section 34-57, but such enumeration shall not be deemed to be exclusive:
(1) Horns and signaling devices. The sounding of any horn or signaling device on any automobile, motorcycle or other vehicle on any street or public place in the city, except as a danger warning; the creation of any unreasonably loud or harsh sound by means of any such signaling device and the sounding of any such device for an unreasonable period of time; the use of any signaling device, except a police whistle or one operated by hand or electricity; the use of any horn, whistle or other device operated by engine exhaust and the use of any such signaling device when traffic is held up for any reason.
(2) Radios, phonographs and other machines which produce or reproduce sound. The playing, using or operating, or permitting to be played, used or operated, of any radio receiving set, musical instrument, phonograph, tape recorder, cassette player, CD player, or other machine or device for the production or reproducing of sound in such manner as to disturb the peace, quiet and comfort of the neighboring inhabitants or pedestrians within any area of the city, or at any time with louder volume than is necessary for convenient hearing for the person who is in the room, vehicle, place or chamber in which such machine or device is operated, and who is a voluntary listener thereto. The operation of any such set, instrument, phonograph, tape recorder, cassette player, CD player, machine or device in such manner as to be plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the building, structure, place or vehicle in which it is located shall be prima facie evidence of a violation of this section.
(3) Loudspeakers and amplifiers for advertising. The playing, using or operating, or permitting to be played, used or operated, of any radio receiving set, musical instrument, phonograph, loudspeaker, sound amplifier or other machine or device for the producing or reproducing of sound which is cast upon the public streets for the purpose of commercial advertising or attracting the attention of the public to any building or structure without a special permit from the city clerk or governing authority. Announcements over loudspeakers can only be made by the announcer in person and without the aid of any mechanical device.
(4) Yelling and shouting. Yelling, shouting, hooting, whistling or singing on the public streets, particularly between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., or at any time or place so as to annoy or disturb the quiet, comfort or repose of any persons in the vicinity.
(5) Animals and birds. The keeping of any animal or bird which will disturb the comfort or repose of any persons in the vicinity by making loud, continual or frequent noise.
(6) Steam whistle. The blowing of any train whistle or steam whistle attached to any stationary boiler, except to give notice of the time to begin or stop work or as a warning of fire or danger or upon request of proper city authorities.
(7) Exhausts. The discharge into the open air of the exhaust of any steam engine, stationary internal combustion engine, motorboat or motor vehicle, except through a muffler or other device which will effectively prevent loud or explosive noises therefrom.
(8) Defect in vehicle or load. The use of any automobile, motorcycle or vehicle so out of repair, so loaded or in such manner as to create loud and unnecessary grating, grinding, rattling or other noise.
(9) Loading, unloading and opening boxes. The creation of a loud and excessive noise in connection with loading or unloading any vehicle or the opening and destruction of bales, boxes, crates and containers.
(10) Construction or repairing of buildings. The erection (including excavating), demolition, alteration or repair of any building other than between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. on weekdays, except on urgent necessity in the interest of public health and safety, and then only with a permit from the city building official, which permit may be granted for a period not to exceed three days or less while the emergency continues and which permit may be renewed by the mayor and council for periods of three days or less while the emergency continues. If the council determines that the public health and safety will not be impaired by the erection, demolition, alteration or repair of any building or the excavation of streets and highways from 6:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m., and further determines that loss or inconvenience would result to any party in interest, the council may grant permission for such work to be done from 6:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m., upon application made at the time the permit for the work is applied for or during the progress of the work.
(11) Noise causing disturbance to schools, courts, churches and hospitals. The creation of any excessive noise on any street adjacent to any school, institution of learning, church or court while such institutions are in session or adjacent to any hospital, and which unreasonably interferes with the work of such institution, or which disturbs or unduly annoys patients in the hospital; provided, however, that conspicuous signs are displayed about such institutions indicating the presence of such institutions.
(12) Hawkers, peddlers and vendors. The shouting and crying of peddlers, hawkers and vendors which disturb the peace and quiet of the neighborhood.
(13) Noises to attract attention; use of drums and other instruments. The use of any drum or other instrument or device for the purpose of attracting attention to any performance, show or sale by creation of noise.
(14) Transportation of metal rails. The transportation of rails, pillars or columns of iron, steel or other material over and along streets and other public places upon carts, drays, cars, trucks or in any other manner so loaded as to cause loud noises or as to disturb the peace and quiet of such streets or other public places.
(15) Piledrivers, hammers or other loud appliances. The operation from 6:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. of any piledriver, steam shovel, pneumatic hammer, derrick, steam or electric hoist or other appliance, the use of which is attended by loud or unusual noise without a special permit from the mayor and council.
(16) Blowers. The operation of any noise-creating blower or power fan or any internal combustion engine, the operation of which causes noise due to the explosion of operating gases or fluids, unless the noise from such blower or fan is muffled and such engine is equipped with a muffler device sufficient to deaden such noise.
(17) Sound trucks. The use of mechanical loudspeakers or amplifiers on trucks or other moving or standing vehicles for advertising or other commercial purposes, and the use of sound trucks for noncommercial purposes during such hours or in such places or with such volume as would constitute such use a public nuisance.
(Code 1984, § 11-1-5; Code 1996, § 42-123; Ord. of 4-2-1991)

The offense of loitering or prowling, as defined in this section, within the city is hereby declared unlawful. A person commits the offense of loitering or prowling when he is in a place at a time or in a manner not usual for law-abiding individuals under circumstances that warrant a justifiable and reasonable alarm or immediate concern for the safety of persons or property in the vicinity. Among the circumstances which may be considered in determining whether alarm is warranted is the fact that the person takes flight upon the appearance of a law enforcement officer, refuses to identify himself, or manifestly endeavors to conceal himself or any object. (4) Marginal access streets means minor streets which are parallel to and adjacent to major streets and highways, and which provide access to abutting properties and protection from through traffic.
(5) Minor streets means those which are used primarily for access to the abutting properties.
Subdivider means any person, corporation or duly authorized agent who undertakes the subdivision of land.
Subdivision.
(1) The term "subdivision" means the division, development or redivision of a lot, tract or parcel of land regardless of how it is to be used into two or more lots either by plat or by metes and bounds description, or the division or redivision of land involving the dedication of a new park, playground, street or other public right-of-way or facility; or the vacation, realignment or any other change in existing streets, alleys, easements, recreational areas, water areas or other public improvements or facilities, and, when appropriate to the context, shall relate to the act or process of subdividing or to the land subdivided.
(2) For the purposes of this chapter, the following are excepted from the term "subdivision":
a. Any subdivision of land for agricultural purposes, provided no lot thereby produced has an area of less than ten acres and an average width of from 400 feet and where no new streets, roads or other rights-of-way are involved.
b. The sale or exchange of parcels of land between owners of adjoining properties, provided that additional lots are not thereby created and that the lots created are not reduced below the minimum sizes required by this chapter or the zoning regulations of the city.
c. The transfer of unsubdivided land or a lot or parcel of land established by deed or plat recorded among the land records of the city prior to the effective date of the regulations from which this chapter was derived.
d. The division or sale of land by judicial decree.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-2; Code 1996, § 78-2)
661:
(a) Conditions. The planning commission shall have authority to vary and modify the provisions of this chapter; provided, however, that in granting variances and modifications, the planning commission may require such conditions as will, in its judgment, secure substantially the objectives of the standards or requirements so varied or modified.
(b) Hardship. Where the planning commission finds that extraordinary hardship may result from strict compliance with the regulations established in this chapter, it may vary the regulations so that substantial justice may be done and the public interest secured; provided, however, that such variation will not have the effect of nullifying the intent and purpose of the master plan or this chapter.
(c) Large-scale development. The standards and requirements of the regulations established in this chapter may be modified in the case of a plan and program for a complete community or a neighborhood unit, which, in the judgment of the planning commission, provides adequate public spaces and improvements for the circulation, recreation, light, air and service needs of the tract when fully developed and populated, and which also provides such covenants or other legal provisions as will ensure conformity to and achievement of the plan.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-3; Code 1996, § 78-3)
665:
(a) Sketch plan. Two copies of the sketch plan shall be required. The sketch plan shall show in sketch form the proposed layout of streets, lots and other features in relation to existing conditions. The sketch plan may be a freehand sketch made directly on a print of the topographic survey, if available. The sketch plan shall include the existing topographic data listed in section 44-26(b) or such data as is necessary for consideration of the proposed sketch plan.

(Code 1984, § 8-5-11; Code 1996, § 78-31)
666:
(a) Preliminary plat. Seven copies of blue-line prints shall be required. The preliminary plat shall be drawn at a scale of not less than 100 feet to one inch. It shall show all existing conditions required in subsection (b) of this section, and shall show all proposals, including the following:
(1) Street names, right-of-way widths, central angles of street intersections, dimensions or radii or chords, approximate grades, and similar data for alleys, if any;
(2) Lot lines, lot numbers and block numbers;
(3) Sites, if any, to be dedicated or reserved for parks, playgrounds or other public uses, together with the purpose and the conditions or limitations of such dedications, if any;
(4) Sites, if any, for multifamily dwellings, shopping centers, churches, industry, or other nonpublic uses exclusive of single-family dwellings; and
(5) Minimum building setback lines.
(b) Existing conditions data. Data required as a basis for the preliminary plat shall include the following information and other pertinent data as required to support the preliminary design of the proposed development:
(1) Boundary lines: Bearings, if available, and distances.
(2) Easements: Location, width and purpose.
(3) Streets on and adjacent to the tract: Name, right-of-way width and location.
(4) Significant contour data at such an interval (maximum of ten feet) as required to determine preliminary design of the proposed improvements and other dependent features.
(5) Other conditions on the tract: Watercourse, existing structures and other significant features.
(6) Title and certificates: Title under which the proposed subdivision is to be recorded, with names of owners and certification of a registered professional civil engineer or registered land surveyor.
(7) Scale, datum, north arrow, date of survey, date of plat and land lot and district numbers.
(c) Draft of protective covenants. One copy of the draft of protective covenants, whereby the subdivider proposes to regulate land use in the subdivision and otherwise protect the proposed development, shall be required.

(Code 1984, § 8-5-12; Code 1996, § 78-32)

The proposed names of the subdivision and proposed street names shall not duplicate or too closely approximate, phonetically, the name of any other subdivision or street in the city.

(b) Protective covenants. Protective covenants, if any, shall be shown on the final plat.

671:
(a) Consultation with building official. Prior to the preparation of the subdivision plat, the subdivider shall confer with the building official, who shall review the sketch plan of the proposed subdivision to determine whether the subdivision meets the requirements of this chapter. This step does not require formal application or filing of the plat with the planning commission.

(Code 1984, § 8-5-21; Code 1996, § 78-51)
672:
(a) Preparation. On reaching conclusions informally, as described in section 44-60, regarding his general program and objectives, the subdivider shall cause to be prepared a preliminary plat, together with other supplementary material as deemed necessary by the building official and specified in section 44-28.
(b) Submission to planning commission. Four copies of the preliminary plat and supplementary material specified, together with two copies of a written letter of application for conditional approval of the preliminary plat, shall be submitted to the planning commission at least seven days prior to the meeting at which it is to be considered.
(c) Conditional approval or disapproval. Within 30 days after the submission of the preliminary plat and other material submitted for consideration, the planning commission shall express its approval as conditional approval and state the conditions of such approval, if any, or if disapproval, shall express its disapproval and its reasons therefor.
(d) Noting of action of planning commission. The action of the planning commission shall be noted on two copies of the preliminary plat, referenced and attached to any conditions determined. One copy shall be returned to the subdivider and the other retained by the planning commission.
(e) Conditional approval not to constitute final approval. Conditional approval of a preliminary plat shall not constitute approval of the final plat. Rather, such conditional approval shall be deemed an expression of approval of the layout submitted on the preliminary plat as a guide to the preparation of the final plat which will be submitted for approval of the planning commission upon fulfillment of the requirements of this chapter and the conditions of the conditional approval, if any.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-22; Code 1996, § 78-52)
673:
A subdivision having five lots or less, with lots fronting a previously dedicated street, and abutting all adjacent properties which have been previously subdivided, and if the platting of the subdivision does not affect any major alterations of utility installation, may be subdivided under the short-form subdivision procedure prescribed as follows:
(1) Preapplication. The preapplication procedure as described in section 44-60 shall be performed.
(2) Design standard and data. The design standard and data of the filing plat of the short-form subdivision shall be identical, when applicable, to those of the long-form subdivision plats.
(3) Preparation of preliminary plat. On reaching conclusions informally, as described in section 44-60, regarding his general program and objectives, the subdivider shall cause to be prepared a preliminary plat together with other supplementary material as deemed necessary by the building official, and specified in section 44-28.
(4) Submission of preliminary plat to building official. Four copies of the preliminary plat and supplementary material specified, together with two copies of a written letter of application for conditional approval, shall be submitted to the building official.
(5) Conditional approval. Conditional approval shall be given to the subdivider by the building official within five days after the submission of the written letter of application, preliminary plat and supplementary material when the proposed subdivision meets the design standards of the subdivision regulations established in this chapter. The action of the building official shall be noted on two copies of the preliminary plat, referenced and attached to any conditions determined. One copy shall be returned to the subdivider and the other retained by the building official.
(6) Preparation of final plat. After obtaining conditional approval from the building official, the subdivider may then proceed to prepare the final plat.
(7) Omission of preliminary submission procedure. The preliminary submission procedure as prescribed in section 44-26 shall be omitted in the short-form subdivision procedure.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-23; Code 1996, § 78-53)
674:
(a) Preparation. The final plat shall be prepared as specified in section 44-28 and shall conform substantially to the preliminary plat, as approved, and if desired by the subdivider, it may constitute only that portion of the approved preliminary plat which he proposes to record and develop at the time; provided, however, that such portion conforms to all requirements of the regulations established in this chapter.
(b) Submission of performance bonds. All performance bonds must be submitted to the city prior to approval of final plat by the planning commission.
(c) Submission of final plat to planning commission. The final plat, and other supplementary material required for approval, shall be submitted to the planning commission at least seven days prior to the meeting at which it is to be considered. It shall also be required that such material shall be submitted to the planning commission within six months after approval of the preliminary plat; otherwise, such approval shall become null and void unless an extension of time is applied for and granted by the planning commission.
(d) Action by planning commission. Within 30 days after the submission of the final plat and supplementary material required for approval, the planning commission shall express its final action.

(Code 1984, § 8-5-24; Code 1996, § 78-54)

(Code 1984, § 8-5-32; Code 1996, § 78-72)

685:

Minor streets shall be so laid out that their use by through traffic will be discouraged.

Where a subdivision abuts or contains an existing or proposed major street, the planning commission may require marginal access streets, reverse frontage with screen planting contained in a non-access reservation along the rear property line, deep lots with rear service alleys, or such other treatment as may be necessary for adequate protection of residential properties and to afford separation of through and local traffic.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-63; Code 1996, § 78-143)

Reserve strips controlling access to streets shall be prohibited except where their control is definitely placed in the city.

Street jogs with centerline offsets of less than 125 feet shall be avoided.

Dead-end streets may be platted where the planning commission deems desirable and where the land adjoins property not subdivided, in which case the streets shall be carried to the boundaries of the land.

No street names shall be used which will duplicate or be confused with the names of existing streets. Street names shall be subject to the approval of the planning commission.

712:
Where a subdivision is traversed by a watercourse, drainageway, natural channel or stream, there shall be provided an easement conforming substantially to the limits of such watercourse, plus additional width as necessary to accommodate future construction as recommended by the building official.

713:
Utility easements shall be avoided except in unusual cases where no other satisfactory arrangements can be provided for the installation of utilities.

714:
Permission must be obtained from the building official for the dedication of utility easements prior to the submission of such dedication.

715:
Pedestrian easements, not less than ten feet wide, may be required where deemed essential to provide circulation or access to schools, playgrounds, shopping centers, transportation and other community facilities.

718:
Proposed subdivisions shall provide appropriate open spaces, suitably located and of reasonable size for parks, playgrounds, play lots, playfields or other recreational areas as may be necessary. (Code 1984, § 8-5-91; Code 1996, § 78-191)
719:
Parks and playgrounds may be dedicated to the city or reserved for public use under private ownership. If so dedicated, the land shall be used exclusively by the city for recreational purposes, and the subdivider may stipulate a reasonable limit of time within which the city is required to make physical improvements to the site, otherwise the title of the site will revert to the subdivider.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-92; Code 1996, § 78-192)
720:
The size and location of parks and playgrounds shall be subject to the approval of the planning commission.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-93; Code 1996, § 78-193)
721:
Where the proposed subdivision is too small to provide space of suitable size for the public open space use intended, the open space provided may be combined with that provided or to be provided in an adjoining area. Thus, in the aggregate, there will be provided an open space of suitable size for the purpose intended.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-94; Code 1996, § 78-194)
722:
Where a site for a public school building is deemed suitable by the planning commission and the proper school authority in a subdivision, such site shall be reserved for public usage. (Code 1984, § 8-5-95; Code 1996, § 78-195)

The subdivider is required to file with the city a performance bond which is available to the city and in sufficient amount to ensure completion of all street and sewer improvements, or, in lieu of such bond, the subdivider may submit performance bonds by contractors for street improvements and sewer construction of the proposed subdivision to ensure such completion of all street and sewer improvements.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-101; Code 1996, § 78-221)
726:
The building official must approve plans for and inspect and approve construction of all subdivision work. The county health department must approve plans for the use of sewerage, septic tanks or other sanitary facilities.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-102; Code 1996, § 78-222)
727:
The subdivider is responsible for maintenance of pavement and the drainage system in the subdivision for a period of one year and is required to post with the city a surety bond in the amount of ten percent of the performance bond required pursuant to section 44-268 to ensure the completion of streets and roads. Such bond shall be valid for a period of one year beginning on the date of final acceptance of the streets by the city.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-103; Code 1996, § 78-223)
728:
If, upon being notified of the failure of the pavement or drainage system, the subdivider does not correct the deficiency or commence work within ten days of the notice, such failure shall be deemed to be a failure on the bond and the city shall have the right to make the necessary repairs, either by public work or by private contract, and the bond shall be liable for the full amount of the cost of the repairs.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-104; Code 1996, § 78-224)
729:
All underground work consisting of sewers, water lines, gas mains and telephone conduits shall be installed and the earth backfill compacted before pavement is laid.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-105; Code 1996, § 78-225)
730:
Two copies of the complete plans and profiles for street improvements shall be submitted for approval of the building official prior to approval of the final plat by the planning commission.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-106; Code 1996, § 78-226)
731:
Street improvements shall be provided in each subdivision as prescribed in the following:
(1) Grading. Grading shall be done by the developer. Streets shall be graded to a width of not less than 42 feet in the center of the right-of-way to provide for a 26-foot pavement and two eight-foot shoulders.
(2) Curbing. Granite or concrete curb shall be furnished by the developer. Any curb damaged after being set and before pavement is completed shall be reset by the developer.
(3) Paving. Pavement shall be furnished and paid for by the developer. Pavement shall consist of four inches of stone, penetrated with two gallons of AC 8 asphalt choked with 35 pounds of Choke Stone No. 89, and topped with 100 pounds of hot plant asphalt per square yard.

(5) Driveways. Driveways from the edge of the pavement to the property line shall be constructed of concrete of six-inch minimum thickness and a 28-day compressive strength of 3,000 psi.

(Code 1984, § 8-5-107; Code 1996, § 78-227)
732:
(a) Required. Sewers shall be laid in all streets, service connections installed to property lines, and connections made to trunk line sewers or a master septic tank.
(b) Septic tanks. Individual septic tanks will be permitted only by special permission of the county health department.

733:
Adequate storm drain pipes and catchbasins shall be installed by developers.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-109; Code 1996, § 78-229)
734:
Water mains shall be laid in all streets and service connections installed to property lines by developers.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-110; Code 1996, § 78-230)
735:
Iron pins of no less than 24 inches long nor less than one-half inch in diameter shall be set flush with the ground at every lot corner.
(Code 1984, § 8-5-111; Code 1996, § 78-231)

State Law reference— Municipalities authorized to levy and collect tax on the furnishing for value to the public of rooms, lodgings or accommodations, O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51.
744:
The following words, terms, and phrases shall, for the purposes of this article and except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning, be defined as follows:
City means the City of Donalsonville and, variously, the incorporated territory of the city wherein the city government is empowered to impose this tax by O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50 et seq.
City clerk means the duly appointed city clerk, other public official, or non-natural person designated by the governing authority to administer the tax.
Due date means the 20th day after the close of the period for which the tax is to be computed.
Folio means primary documentation produced by a hotel that demonstrates interaction between the lodging provider and the occupant, and which, at a minimum, reflects the name and address given by the occupant, the date(s) of occupancy, the amount of rent charged for each date together with the amounts of applicable excise tax, and the method(s) of payment.
Guest room means structural accommodations occupied, or intended, arranged, or designed for transient occupancy, by one or more occupants for the purpose of temporary living quarters.
Hotel means any physical structure or any portion of such a facility, including any house, rooming house, Turkish bath, bachelor hotel, studio hotel, motel, motor hotel, auto or trailer court, truckstop, tourist cabin, campground, lodge, inn, timeshare or other condominium, apartment, public club, or private club, containing guest accommodations and which is occupied, or is intended or designed for temporary occupancy, by paying guests, whether rent is paid in money, goods, labor, or otherwise. It does not include any school dormitory, hospital, asylum, sanitarium, orphanage, jail, prison, or other facility in which human beings are housed and detained under legal restraint.
Lodging provider means:
(1) Any person operating a hotel in the city including, but not limited to, the owner or proprietor of such premises, lessee, sub-lessee, lender in possession, licensee or any other person operating such hotel; and who is subject to the taxation imposed for furnishing for value to the public any rooms, lodgings, or accommodations.
(2) Any person as defined by O.C.G.A. § 48-8-2(8)(M.3) who is subject to the taxation imposed for facilitating the furnishing for value to the public any rooms, lodgings, or accommodations on behalf of another person.
Occupancy means the use or possession, or the right to the use or possession of any guest room in a hotel or the right to the use or possession of the furnishings or to the services and accommodations accompanying the use and possession of the guest room.
Occupant means any person who, for a consideration, uses, possesses, or has the right to use or possess any guest room in a hotel under any lease, concession, permit, right of access, license to use or other agreement, or otherwise.
Permanent resident means any occupant who, as of a given date, has or shall have occupied or has or shall have the right of occupancy of any guest room in a hotel for not less than 30 continuous days next preceding such date.
Person means any natural individual, firm, partnership, joint adventure, association, social club, fraternal organization, joint stock company, corporation, cooperative, estate, trust, receiver, trustee, syndicate, or any other group or combination acting as a unit, the plural as well as the singular number; excepting a franchiser as defined by O.C.G.A. § 48-l3-50.4(i); and the United States and the State of Georgia and any instrumentality of either thereof upon which the city is without power to impose the tax.
Prescribed period means the months and/or quarters of the calendar year as prescribed by the city clerk for return and remittance of the tax. A bifurcated scheme in the best interest of the city's administration shall be permissible provided that such is based upon the reasonable and equitable classification of lodging providers.
Rent means the consideration received for occupancy valued in money, whether received in money or otherwise, including all receipts, cash, credits, and property or services of any kind or nature, and also the amount for which credit is allowed by the lodging provider to the occupant, without any deduction therefrom whatsoever.
Tax means the tax on occupants imposed by this article, as provided for by O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50 et seq., specifically O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50(1).
(Ord. No. 12-1, § 1, 1-3-2011; Ord. No. 08-02-2022, § 1, 9-6-2022)

749:
(a) Due date of taxes. All amounts of such tax shall be due and payable to the city clerk on or before the 20th day of the month next succeeding the respective prescribed period. The tax shall become delinquent for any prescribed period after the 20th day of each succeeding month during which it remains unpaid.
(b) Penalty and interest for failure to pay tax by due date. A lodging provider who fails to make any return or to pay the amount of tax as prescribed, shall be assessed a specific penalty to be added to the tax in the amount of five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, if the failure is for one month or less; and an additional five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, for each additional month or fraction thereof in which such failure shall continue; provided, however, that the aggregate penalty for any single violation shall not exceed 25 percent or $25.00, whichever is greater. Delinquent amounts shall bear interest monthly, or fraction thereof, until paid at the rate set forth in O.C.G.A. § 48-2-40.
(c) Acceptance of delinquent return and remittance without imposing penalty and interest; authority; requirements. If the failure to make any return or to pay the amount of tax by the due date results from providential cause shown to the satisfaction of the governing authority of the city by affidavit attached to the return, and remittance is made within ten days of the due date, such return may be accepted exclusive of penalty and interest.
(d) Waiving of penalty and interest; authority. O.C.G.A. § 48-2-41, relating to the authority to waive interest, and O.C.G.A. § 48-2-43, relating to the authority to waive penalty, shall apply; provided, however, that the governing authority shall stand in lieu of the state commissioner of revenue, and the city shall stand in lieu of the state.
(e) Penalty for fraud. In the case of a false or fraudulent return, or of failure to file a return where willful intent exists to defraud the city of any tax due, a penalty of 50 percent shall be assessed.
(f) Return; remittance; time of filing; lodging providers required to file; contents. On or before the 20th day of the month next succeeding the respective prescribed period, a return for such preceding period together with appropriate remittance shall be filed with the city clerk. The return shall report the gross rent, taxable rent, exempt rent, amount of tax collected or otherwise due for the period, and such other information as may be required by the city clerk.
(g) Extension of time of filing; authority; requirements; remittance; penalty and interest. The governing authority of the city may, for good cause, extend the time for making returns for not longer than 30 days. No extension shall be valid unless granted in writing upon written application of the lodging provider. Such grant may not be applicable for a longer period than 12 consecutive months. A lodging provider granted an extension shall remit tax equaling not less than 100 percent of the tax paid for the corresponding period of the prior fiscal year; such remittance to be made on or before the date the tax would otherwise come due without the grant of extension. No penalty or interest shall be charged during the first ten days of the extension period. Thereafter, interest shall be collected on the unpaid balance at the rate set forth in O.C.G.A. § 48-2-40.
(h) Collection fee allowed lodging providers. Lodging providers collecting the tax shall be allowed a percentage of the tax due and accounted for and shall be reimbursed in the form of a deduction in submitting, reporting and paying the amount due, if the amount is not delinquent at the time of payment. The rate of the deduction shall be three percent of the amount due, but only if the amount due was not delinquent at the time of payment.
(Ord. No. 12-1, § 6, 1-3-2011; Ord. No. 08-02-2022, § 6, 9-6-2022)
750:
(a) Re-computation of tax; authority to make; basis of recomputation. (e) Appeal or protest of deficiency determination. The procedure for contesting a deficiency determination shall be as provided by O.C.G.A. § 48-5-380.

The resale of water purchased from the city is expressly prohibited.
(Code 1984, § 6-1-3; Code 1996, § 90-3)
797:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Commercial means any type of building other than residential.
Construction means the erection of a new building or the alteration of an existing building in connection with its repair or renovation or in connection with making an addition to an existing building and shall include the replacement of a malfunctioning, unserviceable, or obsolete faucet, showerhead, toilet or urinal in an existing building.
Residential means any building or unit of a building intended for occupancy as a dwelling, but shall not include a hotel or motel.
(Code 1996, § 90-31; Ord. of 1-8-1991, § 1)
798:
This article shall be enforced by the office of the city building official. Citations for violations may be issued by the city building official.

800:
The requirements of section 50-27 shall apply to any residential construction and to any commercial construction which involves the repair or renovation of or addition to any existing building when such repair or renovation of or addition to such existing building includes replacement of toilets or showers, or both.
(Code 1996, § 90-36; Ord. of 1-8-1991, § 4)
803:
The chief of police shall be the enforcement authority for this article. The county/city manager may also authorize other departments as may be deemed necessary to support enforcement.
(Ord. of 11-2-2010, § 90-39)
807:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) means the calculated pounds of oxygen required to satisfy the five-day oxygen demand of 1,000,000 pounds of waste when tested in accordance with the procedure given in the latest edition of Standard Methods, published by the American Public Health Association.
Building sewer means that part of the horizontal piping of a building drainage system extending from the outside of the building or end of the inside plumbing system to, and including, the connection with the city sewer system.
City sewer system means such system composed of sanitary sewers, storm sewers, combined sewers, and sewage treatment works owned by a city.
Combined sewer means a sewer intended to receive domestic sewage, treated or weak industrial wastes, surface water and stormwater.
Domestic sewage means liquid from residences, business buildings or institutions which has a daily average of not more than 400 parts per million of BOD and a like amount of suspended solids.
Industrial wastes means the liquid wastes resulting from processes employed in industrial establishments. An industrial waste will be considered weak when it contains less than 600 parts per million of BOD and suspended solids with no biologically toxic substances in it.
pH means a measure of acidity or alkalinity which has a range of zero to 14.
Sanitary sewer means a sewer intended to receive domestic sewage and treated or weak industrial waste without the admixture of surface water, stormwater, or unpolluted industrial process water.
Storm sewer means a sewer intended to receive stormwater and surface water, street wash, or drainage and sewage and industrial wastes that have been completely purified.
Suspended solids means the amount of material in suspension expressed in parts per million as determined by the Gooch crucible method given in the latest edition of Standard Methods, published by the American Public Health Association.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-1; Code 1996, § 90-66)
808:
Whenever it is found that any person is violating any of the provisions or requirements set out in this article, a written notice, stating the offense and setting a time limit for the correction, shall be served upon the offender by the chief of police. The offender shall, within the time limit stated in the notice served upon him, forever cease all violations.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-9(a); Code 1996, § 90-67)
809:
It shall be unlawful for any owner or lessee to place, deposit, or permit to be deposited, any human excrement, garbage or any other organic waste upon the premises in an unsanitary manner.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-2; Code 1996, § 90-69)
810:
It shall be unlawful to discharge any untreated domestic sewage, industrial wastes or other polluted waters into any streams or ditches or any abandoned water well, or in any way to discharge sewage or industrial waste directly into underground waters within the area controlled by the city.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-3; Code 1996, § 90-70)
811:
It shall be unlawful to construct or maintain any privy, privy vault, cesspool or septic tank intended for, or subject to, receiving organic wastes wherever a connection can be made to the city sewer system within 200 feet of any property.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-4; Code 1996, § 90-71)
812:
The owner of all houses, buildings or properties situated within the city, abutting on any streets, alleys or parkways, in which there is now located or may hereafter be located any sewer pipeline of the sanitary sewer system of the city, is hereby required, at his own cost and expense, to install suitable toilet facilities and to connect those houses or buildings erected upon the property directly with the sanitary sewer system within three months after notice to do so.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-5; Code 1996, § 90-72)
813:
Any person owning or controlling premises located beyond the corporate limits of the city and desiring to install a plumbing system on the premises and connect the system with the sanitary sewers of the city may do so by complying with the requirements of this article and by paying a monthly sewer rental charge.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-6; Code 1996, § 90-73)
814:
Where city sewers are not available, or where a connection, as determined by the mayor and council, cannot be made, a septic tank or another method of private sewage disposal must be constructed according to the requirements of the state department of natural resources.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-7; Code 1996, § 90-74)
815:
Authority is hereby granted to the duly authorized city employees to enter upon all properties to make all necessary inspections, tests, and measurements to ensure complete compliance with all of the regulations of this article.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-8; Code 1996, § 90-75)
818:
A separate building sewer is required for each individual building or house, whether constructed as a detached unit or as one or a pair or row, but a single building sewer will be permitted to serve an apartment house or other multiple unit structure or industrial plant whose individual apartments or units are not subject to separate ownership.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-21; Code 1996, § 90-91)
819:
Building sewers from the point of entry of the city sewer to the building shall be laid by the owner at his expense, but only after such connections have been authorized by a permit issued by the superintendent of utilities upon the submission of evidence by the owner that the discharge from the building sewer will comply with all of the regulations of this article.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-22; Code 1996, § 90-92)
820:
Old building sewers and drains may be used in connection with new buildings or new plumbing only when they are approved through issue of a permit as for new construction of building sewers.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-23; Code 1996, § 90-93)
821:
All building sewers shall be not less than six inches in diameter and shall have a fall of not less than one-half inch per foot for six-inch pipe and not less than one-quarter inch per foot for pipe eight inches or over in diameter.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-24; Code 1996, § 90-94)
822:
All pipe shall be laid on a uniform grade and, where possible, on a straight line. Where the building sewer cannot be laid on a straight line, curved pipe shall be used for every deflection from a straight line of more than three inches per foot.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-25; Code 1996, § 90-95)
823:
Where building sewers are within 20 feet of large tree trunks, it is recommended that cast iron pipe with leaded joints be used. All joints must be filled, made smooth and absolutely watertight.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-26; Code 1996, § 90-96)
824:
The connection between the building sewer and the city sewer shall be made at the Y branch provided. If no Y branch was left in the city sewer for the building sewer and the city sewer is not over 12 inches in diameter, a Y branch shall be installed in the city sewer at the desired location by the owner of the building sewer. Where the city sewer is over 12 inches in diameter and where no Y branch was left for the building sewer, a hole may be cut in the city sewer large enough to receive the end of the building sewer and the connection made so that the building sewer enters the city sewer at an angle of 45 degrees. A 45-degree ell can be used to make this connection if the spigot end is cut to fit so that it does not extend past the inside surface of the city sewer. City sewers shall not be tapped below the centerline of the city sewer.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-27; Code 1996, § 90-97)
825:
In backfilling, the material shall be carefully placed and packed around the pipe to provide a uniform bearing and to keep the pipe in proper position. No stones, bricks or like material shall be used in the backfill until there has been a depth of at least 18 inches of fine earth or gravel placed over the pipe.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-28; Code 1996, § 90-98)
826:
Proper barricades and lights must be maintained on the banks of the trenches to guard the public against accidents during construction or connection of the building sewer.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-29; Code 1996, § 90-99)
829:
No stormwater from pavements, areaways, roofs or other sources shall be admitted to the sanitary sewers which are designed to be used exclusively as carriers of domestic sewage and suitable industrial wastes. The same shall apply to unpolluted process or cooling waters.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-41; Code 1996, § 90-116)
830:
Stormwater shall be admitted only to such sewers as are specifically designed as combined sewers or storm sewers.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-42; Code 1996, § 90-117)
831:
No person shall discharge into any sewer any liquid or gas having a temperature greater than 100 degrees Fahrenheit.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-43; Code 1996, § 90-118)
833:
(a) Required in certain instances. Every building sewer discharging industrial wastes from any plant or establishment into the city sewer system may be required, at the discretion of the approving authorities, to have a sampling manhole for the purpose of ascertaining the quality and quantity of the waste flowing in the building sewer.
(b) Location; construction. The manhole shall be located at a suitable and satisfactory location and it shall be not less than three feet in inside diameter and built in a manner designated by the superintendent of utilities.
(c) Cost. The cost of the manhole shall be borne by the applicant, but the manhole shall become the property of the city government.
(d) Maintenance. The responsibility for maintaining the manhole in a safe condition shall be assumed and remain with the owner of the property at all times.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-45; Code 1996, § 90-120)
834:
Whenever the industrial wastes do not meet the requirements of this article, or the quantity of biochemical oxygen demand is one-tenth of the total of the entire wastes of the city, the industry will be required to pretreat its waste or enter into a one-year agreement with the city to treat the waste as discharged.
(Code 1984, § 6-2-46; Code 1996, § 90-121)
837:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Damage means the substantial weakening of structural or lateral support of an underground utility, penetration or destruction of any protective coating, housing or other protective device of an underground utility, and the partial or complete severance of an underground utility.
Demolish or demolition means any operation by which a structure or mass of material is wrecked, razed, rendered, moved or removed by means of any tool, equipment or discharge of explosives.
Excavate or excavation means an operation for the purpose of the movement or removal of earth, rock or other materials in or on the ground by use of mechanized equipment or by discharge of explosives, and including augering, backfilling, digging, drilling, grading, plowing-in pulling-in, ripping, scraping, trenching and tunneling, but not including the tilling of soil for agricultural purposes.
Mechanized equipment means equipment operated by means of mechanical power, including trenchers, bulldozers, power shovels, augers, backhoes, scrapers, drills, cable and pipe plows and other equipment used for plowing in or pulling in cable or pipe.
Operator means any city or utility commission who owns or operates a utility.
Utility means any line, system or facility used for producing, storing, conveying, transmitting or distributing communication, electricity, gas, petroleum, petroleum products, hazardous liquids, water, steam or sewage.
Working day means every day, except Saturdays, Sundays and national and legal state holidays.
(Code 1984, § 6-3-1; Code 1996, § 90-141)
838:
A permit issued pursuant to the law authorizing excavation or demolition operations shall not be deemed to relieve a person from the responsibility for complying with the provisions of this article.
(Code 1984, § 6-3-2; Code 1996, § 90-143)
839:
Except as provided in section 50-142, no person may excavate in a street, highway, public space, or a private easement of an operator, or near the location of a utility installed on the premises of a customer served by such utility, or demolish a building, without having first ascertained, in the manner prescribed in sections 50-140 and 50-141, the location of all underground utilities in the area that would be affected by the proposed excavation or demolition. Each operator shall maintain a list of all underground utilities and plants or maps showing their location.
(Code 1984, § 6-3-3; Code 1996, § 90-144)
840:
(a) Except as provided in section 50-142, before commencing any excavation or demolition operation designated in section 50-139, each person responsible for such excavation or demolition shall serve written or telephone notice of intent to excavate or demolish at least three but not more than ten full working days to the state utility protection center prior to any such excavation or demolition.
(b) The written or telephonic notice required by subsection (a) of this section must contain the name, address and telephone number of the person filing the notice of intent, and, if different, the person responsible for the excavation or demolition, the starting date, anticipated duration and type of excavation or demolition operation to be conducted, the location of the proposed excavation or demolition, and whether or not explosives are to be used.
(c) If notification required by this section is made by telephone, an adequate record of such notification shall be maintained by the superintendent at the city hall.
(Code 1984, § 6-3-4; Code 1996, § 90-145)
841:
Each operator or designated representative notified in accordance with section 50-140 shall, not less than two working days in advance of the proposed excavation or demolition, unless a shorter period is provided by agreement between the person responsible for the excavation or demolition and the operator or designated representative, supply, by use of maps when appropriate, the following information to the person responsible for the excavation or demolition:
(1) The approximate location and description of all of its underground utilities which may be damaged as a result of the excavation or demolition;
(2) The location and description of all utility markers indicating the approximate location of the underground utilities; and
(3) Any other information that would assist that person in locating and thereby avoiding damage to the underground utilities, including providing adequate temporary marking indicating the approximate location of the underground utility in locations where permanent utility markers do not exist.
(Code 1984, § 6-3-5; Code 1996, § 90-146)
842:
Compliance with the notice requirements of section 50-140 is not required of persons responsible for emergency excavation or demolition to ameliorate an imminent danger to life, health or property; provided, however, that such persons give, as soon as practicable, oral notice of the emergency excavation or demolition to each operator having underground utilities located in the area where such excavation or demolition is to be performed and requests emergency assistance from each operator so identified in locating and providing immediate protection to its underground utilities. An imminent danger to life, health, or property exists whenever there is a substantial likelihood that loss of life, health, or property will result before the procedures under sections 50-140 and 50-141 can be fully complied with.
(Code 1984, § 6-3-6; Code 1996, § 90-147)
843:
(a) Except as provided by subsection (b) of this section, each person responsible for any excavation or demolition operation designated in section 50-139 that results in any damage to an underground utility shall, immediately upon discovery of such damage, notify the operator of such utility of the location and nature of the damage and shall allow the operator reasonable time to accomplish necessary repairs before completing the excavation or demolition in the immediate area of such utility.
(b) Each person responsible for any excavation or demolition operation designated in section 50-139 that results in damage to an underground utility permitting the escape of any flammable, toxic or corrosive gas or liquid shall, immediately upon discovery of such damage, notify the operator, police and fire departments, and take any other action as may be reasonably necessary to protect persons and property and to minimize the hazards until the arrival of the operator's personnel or police and fire departments.
(Code 1984, § 6-3-8; Code 1996, § 90-148)
844:
In addition to the notification requirements of section 50-140, each person responsible for any excavation or demolition operation designated in section 50-139 shall:
(1) Plan the excavation or demolition to avoid damage to or minimize interference with underground utilities in and near the construction area;
(2) Maintain a clearance between an underground utility and the cutting edge or point of any mechanized equipment, taking into account the known limit of control of such cutting edge or point, as may be reasonably necessary to avoid damage to such utility; and
(3) Provide such support for underground utilities in and near the construction area, including during backfill operations, as may be reasonably necessary for the protection of such utilities.
(Code 1984, § 6-3-7; Code 1996, § 90-149)
847:
The city shall collect a fee of five percent of the operator's gross revenues as provided by law, for any cable or video state franchise issued in the corporate boundaries by the state pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 36-76-1 et seq., known as the "Consumer Choice for Television Act" of 2007.
(Res. of 7-1-2008)
854:
Any automobile marked, labeled or identified by lettering or numbers as a taxicab and found upon the streets of the city, or regularly used for transportation of passengers, shall be presumed to be used as a taxicab and for transportation of passengers for hire, for the purpose of this article.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-47; Code 1996, § 94-31)
855:
(a) All motor vehicles operated as taxicabs in the city shall be marked on the outside with the following information:
(1) The name of the owner;
(2) The word "taxicab" or "taxi";
(3) If a fleet or more than one taxicab is operated by one company or owner, a number shall be assigned to each vehicle, which shall be individual and identifying; and
(4) Any other information which may be deemed necessary by the mayor and council.
(b) The markings described in subsection (a) of this section shall be stenciled or painted on each side of the taxicab in a permanent paint of contrasting color to the color of the vehicle or affixed by decal or some like manner. The letters of such markings shall not be less than three inches in height and must be printed so that the markings may be easily read at a distance of at least 50 feet.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-21; Code 1996, § 94-32)
856:
The owner and operator of each taxicab licensed to operate within the city shall, before having his license either granted or renewed, produce to the city manager a written inspection report from a qualified automobile mechanic engaged in business within the city. Such mechanic shall be approved by the mayor and council, showing that the brakes and lights on each unit operated by him are in safe, serviceable condition. The license shall in no case be granted until this section is complied with.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-22; Code 1996, § 94-33)
857:
(a) Notice required. If any owner or operator of a taxicab in the city shall sell, trade or exchange any taxicab being operated in the city and substitute another car therefor, it shall be the duty of the seller to notify the city clerk within ten hours of the sale, trade or exchange of the vehicle, giving the number under which the car traded is identified in the policy of liability insurance on file with the mayor and council.
(b) Transfer of insurance required. It shall also be the duty of such owner or operator of the car substituted to furnish the clerk written endorsement of the insurance company issuing the public liability policy, the endorsement to be attached as an endorsement on the liability policy, showing that the car substituted is insured under the terms of the liability insurance.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-23; Code 1996, § 94-34)
858:
No person shall drive a taxicab upon the streets of the city who is less than 19 years of age.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-24; Code 1996, § 94-35)
859:
No person shall drive a taxicab upon the streets of the city who has been convicted of an offense constituting a felony or who has pleaded guilty upon a charge of having committed an offense constituting a felony.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-25; Code 1996, § 94-36)
860:
It shall be unlawful for any person licensed to drive a taxicab under the provisions of this article to operate such taxicab while he is under the influence of intoxicating liquor. A violation of this section shall be grounds for license revocation.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-26; Code 1996, § 94-37)
861:
(a) Prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person operating a licensed taxicab service in the city, or any driver operating a taxicab in the city under the license, to knowingly haul wine, liquor or beer in such taxicab, provided that this section shall not apply to a driver transporting a fare-paying passenger in possession of alcoholic beverages so long as such alcoholic beverages remain in the possession and control of the passenger and are not opened within the vehicle.
(b) Revocation of license. If the driver of any taxicab in the city knowingly allows or permits intoxicating liquor, wine or beer to be hauled in the taxicab operated by him in violation of this section, the license issued by the city shall automatically be revoked. If any license is forfeited and revoked because a driver is guilty of hauling intoxicating liquor, wine or beer, and desires to be heard, he shall have a right to appeal to the mayor and council for a hearing and be heard at such time and place as the mayor and council shall designate. Pending the hearing before the mayor and council, the licensee shall not operate the taxicab service under and by virtue of any such license.
(c) Forfeiture of driver's rights. It shall be unlawful for any driver guilty of knowingly hauling liquor, wine or beer in any taxicab driven by him to again drive a taxicab in the city.

862:
No person shall drive a taxicab upon the streets of the city when such vehicle contains more persons than such vehicle is designed to carry.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-28; Code 1996, § 94-39)
863:
Drivers of taxicabs shall not receive or discharge passengers in the roadway but shall drive to the sidewalk or curb on the right-hand side of such roadway, and there receive or discharge passengers.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-29; Code 1996, § 94-40)
866:
It shall be unlawful to drive a taxicab or vehicle of any kind for the purpose of transporting passengers or property for hire without first applying for and obtaining an occupational license therefor.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-1; Code 1996, § 94-56)
867:
It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of furnishing taxicab service in the city and maintaining a place of business in the city without first obtaining a license approved by the mayor and council.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-9; Code 1996, § 94-57)
868:
Application for a taxicab driver's license shall be made in such manner and form as prescribed by the city manager.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-2; Code 1996, § 94-58)
870:
No license shall be issued to drive a taxicab until the application has been approved by the city manager.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-4; Code 1996, § 94-60)
871:
The applicant shall submit himself personally before the city manager, if required, or if he so desires, at the time the application for a taxicab driver's license is considered.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-5; Code 1996, § 94-61)
872:
If, upon a consideration of an application for a license to drive a taxicab, the city manager shall decide that the applicant is qualified and entitled to operate a taxicab and in all manners in full compliance with all local, state and federal laws, having due regard to the safety and morals of the public, the application shall be granted and a license issued by the city clerk, upon payment of the business or occupation tax legally demandable. If the city manager shall determine that the applicant is not a fit and proper person to be so licensed, having due regard for the safety and morals of the public, the mayor and council shall refuse such license.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-6; Code 1996, § 94-62)
873:
(a) The city manager shall have authority to suspend or revoke any and all licenses issued under this article, for good cause shown, or in the event the licensee fails to maintain compliance with any local, state or federal law relevant to the operation of the licensed business, after five days' notice given the licensee, at either a regular or special meeting. It shall be unlawful for any licensee to operate during the period of suspension.
(b) The term "good cause" shall mean any violation of this Code or of any state statutes pertaining to the operation of motor vehicles.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-10; Code 1996, § 94-65)

It is the declared policy of the mayor and council that, in licensing the operation of vehicles under this article, a reasonable service will be rendered to the general public and to the inhabitants of the city by the persons holding those licenses, and if such service cannot or will not be rendered by any person holding such license, the license should be revoked. Among the causes justifying such revocation shall be unreasonable failure or refusal to render such service.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-12; Code 1996, § 94-67)
877:
It shall be unlawful to operate upon the public roads, streets and highways within the corporate limits of the city any taxicab which is subject to the regulations and ordinances of the city unless such operation is done in conformity to this division with respect to insurance protection.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-41; Code 1996, § 94-86)
878:
Before using or operating any taxicab which is subject to the provisions of this division for transporting passengers, and before allowing any other person to do so within the city upon the roads, streets and highways, the owner shall provide for each vehicle to be so used, and for the benefit of any and all persons having claims against the owner for damage by way of loss of life, damage to property, and/or for injury to the person, minimum liability insurance coverage as follows:

Minimum personal injury coverage for injuries | $100,000.00

879:
Insurance coverage required by this division shall be subject to approval by the city manager and shall be with a company satisfactory to the city manager and in a form satisfactory to the city manager.

880:
It shall be the duty of the owner to deposit such policies with the city manager, where they shall remain while in force.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-44; Code 1996, § 94-89)
881:
It shall be the duty of the insurer to give reasonable notice to the city before cancelling any coverage. Any company failing to do so will not be considered an acceptable company for the purpose of furnishing such coverage.
(Code 1984, § 9-3-45; Code 1996, § 94-90)

885:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Accessory use means a use customarily incidental, and subordinate to, the principal use or building and located on the same lot with such principal use or building.
Advertising sign, outdoor, means a structural poster panel or painted sign, either freestanding or attached to the outside of a building, for the purpose of conveying information, knowledge, or ideas to the public about a subject either related or unrelated to the premises upon which located.
Alteration means any change in the supporting members of a building (such as bearing walls, beams, columns or girders) except such change as may be required for its safety; any addition to a building; any change in use from that of one district classification to another; or any change of a building from one location to another.
Building means any structure having a roof supported by columns or by walls and intended for shelter, housing or enclosure of persons, animals or chattels. The term "building" includes the term "structure."
Building, accessory, means a building subordinate, or supplemental to, the main building on a lot and used for purposes customarily incidental to that of a main or principal building and located on the same lot therewith.
Building, principal, means a building in which is conducted the main use of the lot on which the building is located.
Business sign means an attached or freestanding structure which directs attention to a business or profession conducted on the premises.
Centerline of street means the line surveyed and monumented by the mayor and council as such or, if a centerline has not been surveyed and monumented, it shall be that line running midway between the outside curbs or ditches of the street.
Customary home occupation means an occupation or profession customarily carried on by an occupant of a dwelling unit as a secondary use which is clearly incidental to the dwelling unit for residential purposes, and carried on wholly within the principal building, and provided that not more than 30 percent of the floor area of the principal building is used for such purposes.
Dwelling means a building designed, arranged, or used for a permanent living quarters for one or more persons.
Dwelling unit means a building, or portion of a building, providing complete living facilities for one family.
Family means one or more persons occupying a dwelling and living as a single house-keeping unit.
Lot means a portion or parcel of land devoted to a common use or occupied by a building or group of buildings devoted to a common use, together with the customary accessories and open spaces belonging to the same. The term "lot" includes the term "plot" or "parcel."
Lot, depth of, means the mean horizontal distance between the front and rear lot lines, measured in the general direction of the side lot lines.
Lot, width of, means the distance between side lot lines measured at the building line.
Map means the zoning map of the city on file in the office of the building official.
Nonconforming use means a building, structure or use of land existing at the time of enactment of the ordinance from which this chapter was derived, and which does not conform to the regulations of the district in which it is located.
Sight distance means the length of roadway visible to the driver of a passenger vehicle at any given point on the roadway when the view is unobstructed by traffic.
Street means a public or private way which affords the principal means of access to abutting properties.
Structure means anything constructed or erected, the use of which requires location on the ground, or attachment to something having location on the ground.
Used or occupied, as applied to any land or building, includes the words "intended, arranged or designed to be used or occupied."
Yard means a space on the same lot with a principal building open, unoccupied and unobstructed by buildings or structures from ground to sky, except where encroachments and accessory buildings are expressly permitted.
Yard, front, means an open, unoccupied space on the same lot with a principal building, extending the full width of the lot, and situated between the street and the front line of the building projected to side lines of the lot.
Yard, rear, means an open, unoccupied space on the same lot with a principal building, extending the full width of the lot and situated between the rear line of the lot and the rear line of the building projected to side lines of the lot.
Yard, side, means an open, unoccupied space on the same lot with a principal building, situated between the building and the side lot line of the lot and extending from the front yard to the rear yard. Any lot line not a rear line or a front line shall be deemed a side line.
(Code 1984, §§ 8-6-2, 8-6-3; Code 1996, § 98-1)
